<thought>The 13C NMR spectrum shows peaks at 169.52, 132.43, 130.27, 129.30, 126.70, 126.66, 123.57, 43.30, and 26.29 ppm. Methyl carbons typically appear in the 10–30 ppm region; only the 26.29 ppm signal falls in that range, indicating a single CH₃ carbon. The 43.30 ppm signal is more consistent with a methylene or carbon attached to an electronegative group, not a methyl. Therefore, the molecule contains one methyl group.</thought>
<final_answer>1</final_answer>
